questions.stem: Products have total S = 300, reactants 260 J/mol K; find delta S (J/mol K).
questions.explanation: For a standard reaction entropy from tabulated molar entropies question like this, the governing rule is: Subtract reactants. Applying it gives "40" as the answer.

questions.topic: Standard Gibbs energy from reaction enthalpy and entropy
questions.learningObjective: Compute delta G at different temperature
questions.stem: Given delta H = -60 kJ/mol, delta S = -150 J/mol K, find delta G at 400 K (kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: The rule that settles this standard gibbs energy from reaction enthalpy and entropy item is: Delta H minus T delta S. That is why "0" is the answer.
questions.hint: Delta H minus T delta S.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: Temperature at which a reaction stops being spontaneous
questions.learningObjective: Determine spontaneity at given temperature
questions.stem: For delta H = +40 kJ/mol, delta S = +100 J/mol K, is reaction spontaneous at 300 K?

options.misconception: selects "Never spontaneous" instead of "No, delta G positive"
names "Yes, delta G negative" where the rule requires "No, delta G positive"
confuses "Always spontaneous" with the correct "No, delta G positive"

questions.explanation: Delta G = 40 - 300*0.1 = 40 - 30 = +10 kJ/mol, positive, so not spontaneous at 300 K. Threshold is 400 K.

questions.topic: Le Chatelier response to compression
questions.learningObjective: Predict shift when removing product
questions.stem: Removing a product from a gaseous equilibrium shifts equilibrium toward?

options.misconception: extreme — treating "Complete reactants" as the answer
names "No shift" where the rule requires "Products"

questions.explanation: Removing product disturbs equilibrium; system produces more product to replace it. Shift is toward products.

questions.topic: Equilibrium extent of a reaction solved by bisection
questions.learningObjective: Explain why bisection needs a sign change
questions.stem: Explain why bisection requires the function to change sign over the interval.

answer.exemplar: By the intermediate value theorem, a continuous function changing sign must have a root in the interval.

questions.explanation: Bisection relies on the intermediate value theorem. A continuous function with opposite signs at endpoints must cross zero somewhere inside.
